chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

The woman with irregular bleeding (mustahadha) counts her waiting period by the blood if it occurs during her usual menstrual days, or by the months if she has a regular monthly cycle. If it is mixed up and she does not know her menstrual days from other bleeding, that is not hidden, because menstrual blood is thick and warm, and the blood of the irregular bleeder is yellow and cool.

Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And if she is pregnant, her waiting period is that she gives birth to her pregnancy, even if it is after divorce by a moment, and she becomes permissible to her husbands. This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted: 'And those who are pregnant, their term is that they deliver their pregnancy.' God Almighty made their waiting period the delivery of the pregnancy, and that is explicit in what we said, and also he has narrated.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: A woman experiencing irregular uterine bleeding (istihadah) distinct from menstruation

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine the waiting period for a woman with irregular bleeding or pregnancy?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on the diagnostic criteria for istihadah by distinguishing the hot, thick nature of menstrual blood from the cold, yellowish discharge of irregular bleeding, a key method in Shia fiqh for determining purity. He further clarifies that the iddah for a pregnant woman concludes immediately upon delivery, even if it occurs shortly after divorce, citing the explicit Quranic mandate in Surah At-Talaq. This narration underscores the practical application of Quranic verses in resolving specific legal ambiguities regarding women's ritual status.
